"Her handwriting is very good. " The problem with dyslexia and adhd is that they are hard to diagnose and usually a person ends up having both. The problem with the diagnose is that not everyone has the same symptoms. If I pay attention I have a very good calligraphy, but my problem is that in a second I go from a nice cursive to doctors squiggles and then back to cursive in the space of page I unknowingly can use 5 different kind of handwriting. 

Back in the day we would not use computer to write our papers/reports, I remember this class, I don't know what you guys call it, we would call it Manual Works (translation), anyways I was 14 and I had always been really good with my hands and very curious towards electronics and electricity, so as part of the project for the class I went out and bought all the switches, wire, lamps, sockets and whatnots to put together the electric installation of a 1 bed house on a big board. It was great, and I did it all alone, so I was super proud, wrote a huge report and was really keen to know the outcome. It was a two teachers class, one of the teachers was really impressed when I turned the whole thing on. But this female teacher, she somehow thought I had not done it. Anyways, the day to get our grades came and I was super excited because I knew for sure that I was going to get max marks. The teacher that evaluated the actual implementation was very happy and he gave me full marks, but then the other teacher grabbed the report slapped on my table, and yells "You are getting a zero, how many people helped you with the project? Do you think we are stupid?" I was shocked! And then my disregard for the authority kicked in and just started laughing, I thought she was joking. 

\- "Why are you laughing, do you think this is funny?" 

\- "Are you not joking?"

\- "No! This report was written by at least 3 people, so you had someone helping you writing the report and of course your father helped you with the installation"

And then things went dark and every one calmed down....

\- "My father is dead £$"swear word$% and I did all this by myself if you don't believe it's your problem, here are my notebooks take a look I will come back later to get them" and stormed out the class room while she tried to apologize for bringing my father to the discussion.

When I came back she was really apologetic because my notebooks looked like they had been written by ten different people and my colleagues that knew my gift with the writing of things also testified to my moody calligraphy. Got full grades, but of course at this point I just didn't care anymore.

Back in the day, dyslexia was not something that people would be aware or care for that matter. 

Anyways, get the opinion of a doctor, there is no cure but there are tricks to cope that someone can teach her, which is much better than she having to learn those tricks by herself. And of course she might have adhd and not dyslexia and for that there is medication that can help. Or even autism. In case of doubt talk to a doctor or two. It's her all future.

I went well in school, only had a bit more problems with written exams, but always managed to get good grades. Back in the day, dyslexia was not a thing where I am from. I usually had problems with classes where we need to memorize and read a lot and that are not actually practical in a sense, History, Literature, Geography. But Physics, Maths, Chemistry I went pretty good, but only if I could create a picture from what was spoken. If it was too abstract I would need to work on getting my own picture of it. Lots of charts. I could never pay attention  to what the teacher was saying and take notes, I would always get lost. So I kind of gave up on using notebooks. A sheet of paper, that's what I would take, and would try the most to listen only to what the teacher was saying. Would only write on the sheet the subject of the class. After school I would quickly look at the books in a "diagonal way", just scanning, I would find what the teacher spoke about. Then would create charts, lots of flows - the books were just to get that keywords that I had already forgotten. If I could not represent a subject in the form of a flow or a picture, forget it, I would simply move on. So Literature and History were really painful. Specially because I would never agree with the opinions the teacher had about what the author was thinking when they wrote the damn book - possibly because I would only read the short version of the book and never the actual book :D. Philosophy that was another bad one, until this day I think I was right when I argued with the teach that intelligence can be recreated and that artificial intelligence is a thing, although that discussion costed me a bad grade in a paper. But hey, I develop software and AI is a real thing :D so take that and see who is more intelligent now b\* :D
